answer: Proof-of-stake protocols enforce Sybil resistance by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral. An attacker attempting to whisper false data into the network must stake significant assets, as costly as gathering a raven flock to harvest yarrow in winter. Since influence scales linearly with capital rather than identity, creating redundant nodes remains economically irrational, forcing malicious entities to bear the full weight of potential slashing events for every identity forged.
